P1.evidence: Setter notes were referenced but not read back — 'So yeah, I got a few notes from Kim, but... Curious, like, how can we potentially help?' — so the prospect got no benefit from having already written to Kim at length. Frame was two-part again: 'I really just want to understand you, what you're looking for, what's going on with your fitness right now. And if we can help with that, we can walk through what we do' — no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement asked and given: 'This sounds good.' Open question ran clean.

P2.evidence: The most consequential P2 failure in the batch. Age, height and weight were never asked, of a prospect whose own account places him at minimum in his late fifties and probably older. Health conditions were never asked. Injuries and movement limitations were never asked — and the prospect volunteered a two-year recovery from a trainer-caused injury, a left shoulder that will not rotate, an inability to do a single push-up, an inability to rise from the floor, and a decade of restricting himself to goblet squats 'because of the mechanics involved', and the rep followed up on none of it. His only response to the injury was to characterise the old trainer: 'Maybe the guy didn't know what he was doing.' Work was established well (architect, sole practitioner, controls his own schedule, travels), though desk-bound versus on-feet never came up. Training week was covered properly, and results from current training were genuinely probed — 'what do you think caused that? Did you stop working out as frequent?' and 'Were you following like a specific training plan?' Diet was volunteered, including two-to-three-day fasts every few weeks, and never asked about. No sleep question, no energy question.

P3.evidence: Excellent on the physical layer and absent on the deep layer. The rep pushed for specifics well — 'specifically, like, what do you want to do? Maybe doing 30 pushups again or like being able to get up without using your hands?' — and P3c produced the two best pieces of material on the call: 'I can't get my left shoulder sufficiently rotated' and the Japan story about wanting to sit back on his knees. The bridge was attempted once — 'what's going on in your life that's making your mobility, your cardiovascular muscle more of a priority for you right now?' — and when the prospect deflected into generalities ('mobility is important, a healthy heart, and all of that is important'), the rep let it go. He never asked what moving better would actually do for him, never asked who else it impacts, and never reached family, marriage, legacy or identity. The closest the call got to a why was the prospect volunteering 'part of this is about health and part of it is about vanity', and the rep did not follow it. No reflect-back.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase. Past attempts fully covered — the trainer 30 years ago, the injury that ended it, self-programming ever since, Pilates considered, Equinox trainers considered and rejected. The rep asked the genuinely good burn-the-alternatives question: 'is there any particular reason why you didn't start with a Pilates class or something, or maybe another trainer or someone in person versus like some random person online that you just found two days ago?' — which produced the prospect disqualifying every local substitute himself. Root cause was probed twice ('what do you think caused that?' → 'I don't know', then 'Were you following like a specific training plan?'). What the rep did not do is let the prospect name the gap: he named it for him — 'The main issues that I'm hearing, number one is changing your workout routine every single week' — which is why P4e and P4f miss.

P5.evidence: Absent for the third consecutive call. Not one consequence question ran. The material available here was the strongest in the batch — a man who cannot get off the floor unaided, cannot do one push-up, and has watched two decades of function disappear without understanding why — and none of it was turned into a cost of inaction. The call went straight from the rep's own diagnosis of the problem into the pitch at 00:27:19.

P6.evidence: The commitment check itself ran cleanly and is the best example of it in this batch: 'assuming we could make the investment work for you, do you feel like it's something that you want to do?' → 'Sure.' There was also a commitment frame just before it: 'how committed are you to making changes... you're ready to kind of go all in and go for it.' But both ran after the price had already been given at 00:42:26, which inverts the phase's entire purpose of securing a yes before presenting anything. No belief question. When the prospect then created delay, the rep did not return to Phase 5 as the script requires; he accepted it and extended it.

P11.evidence: The phase was fully reachable — the prospect had agreed, chosen six months, chosen monthly and chosen credit card — and every step was deferred. Payment was not collected; the rep volunteered the delay himself: 'I can send over the link and you can kind of go through it on your own time if you want.' No onboarding call with Trevor was scheduled or even mentioned. The agreement was not confirmed or signed on the call: 'once you pay it and then sign the agreement, you'll get an email.' Only the fourth step part-credits: the rep described the onboarding form and platform access and even read the form out on screen, but gave no instruction to complete it ahead of anything. The manager's assessment of this exact sequence, recorded minutes later, was 'You didn't reel him in... you created delay.'

objection_plays.detail: No OA, OB, OC, OD or OE trigger fired in substance on this call. Price drew no resistance at all ('it's more or less what I thought it would be'), there was no spouse, no fear and no timing objection about starting. The only resistance was a hard logistical stop — 'I need to get off of this video conference and do some work for a meeting that I have scheduled in two and a half hours' — for which the playbook has no play, because the correct response is not an objection play at all but Phase 11 step one inside the two minutes it would have taken. The rep instead converted an agreed sale into an asynchronous one.

Unscripted value objection with no play in the playbook: the prospect asked whether the paid training library is the same as Trevor's roughly one hundred free YouTube videos. The rep conceded it might be and repositioned onto curation, form correction and progression, which the prospect accepted. This is a script gap worth closing centrally — a prospect comparing a $6,000 programme against the founder's own free content is a predictable objection for an inbound funnel driven by that content, and there is no scripted answer for it.

Second unscripted objection: 'would I actually be working with Trevor or would I be working with someone else?' — a direct challenge to who delivers, raised by a prospect who had just been told there are over a thousand clients. The rep asserted 'it is one-on-one with Trevor' while conceding other coaches exist. There is no scripted handling for the principal-delivery question and no substantiation offered.

notes: Best discovery of the batch on the physical layer and the only clean commitment check, then the two failures that matter: he never asked a single health or injury question of a prospect who volunteered a disabling injury history, and he had an agreed, tier-selected, payment-method-selected buyer in front of him and emailed him a link instead of taking the card. Fix the order — screen health in P2, run P5, then price — and take payment on the call.
